content: Surf Life Saving New Zealand (SLSNZ) is the organization responsible for overseeing surf life-saving activities across New Zealand. Their motto, In it for life, reflects both the enduring commitment of their members to the organization and their dedication to preserving lives by preventing drowning incidents. The primary mission of SLSNZ is to safeguard individuals from drowning and injuries in New Zealand. Surf life-saving clubs patrol specific beaches, with patrolled areas marked by yellow and red flags. Beachgoers are advised to remain within these flagged zones. Remarkably, as of November 2005, no one has drowned while swimming between the flags. SLSNZ operates as the National Association representing nine districts and approximately 70 surf life-saving clubs, with a membership base of around 13,000 individuals. The organization follows a hierarchical membership structure, where club members are automatically members of their respective district and SLSNZ. SLSNZ collaborates directly with the nine districts, which in turn work with individual clubs. A national framework provides guidance and protection to members. Governance is managed by a board of six members elected by the districts. The board appoints a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), who implements an annual management plan to align with the board's strategies, ensuring the organization fulfills its purpose of preventing drowning and injuries. The management team, based in Wellington, supports the CEO in executing the management plan within their specific portfolios. SLSNZ also maintains annual funding agreements with each district. In New Zealand, surf life-saving serves as both a sport and a community service. Participation in either aspect requires club membership and the attainment of the entry-level qualification, the Surf Lifeguard Award. Additional qualifications are available through SLSNZ, including advanced lifesaving certificates, Inflatable Rescue Boat (IRB) qualifications, VHF radio certifications, and first aid training. Volunteer lifeguards patrol beaches and engage with the public to prevent incidents. During the summer of 2005, volunteers conducted over 100,000 preventative actions during 155,000 hours of beach patrols. Competitive events are held at club, district, and national levels, with age categories such as Under 14, Under 19, and Open. These events test rescue skills, strength, fitness, and agility in activities like swimming, running, paddling surf skis, boards, or canoes, and rowing surf boats. Racing Inflatable Rescue Boats has become an increasingly popular aspect of the sport. The NZ Surf League is a televised national Under 19 and Open inter-district competition held in March. SLSNZ generates an annual income of approximately $6 million through sponsorships, gaming machine grants, the NZ Lottery Grants Board, and individual donations. The total income for the organization, including districts and clubs, is around $13 million. SLSNZ does not impose a national membership levy but instead provides programs and distributes over $2 million annually. Recently, SLSNZ has begun offering first aid training to the general public, both to support their mission of preventing drowning and injuries and as a means of generating additional revenue.
